title: The secret worth an empire
text: For centuries silk {{1}} woven only in China, where the recipe was treated as a state secret so valuable {{2}} exporting the eggs of the silkworm was punishable by death. {{3}} was not until the sixth century AD that the secret escaped. According to the story, the emperor Justinian sent two Persian monks east, {{4}} returned with silkworm eggs hidden {{5}} hollow walking canes. {{6}} monopoly broken, Byzantium built its own luxury industry, and over the following centuries silk weaving spread to Baghdad, Sicily and eventually Florence. {{7}} was the demand for the fabric that cities grew rich merely by handling it, and the overland trade route owes its English name {{8}} this one material: the Silk Road.

gaps.hint: passive: silk ___ woven only in China
gaps.explanation: Past passive with an uncountable subject: was woven.

gaps.hint: conjunction: so valuable ___ exporting was punishable
gaps.explanation: 'So valuable that' — degree plus result clause.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ was not until the sixth century
gaps.explanation: 'It was not until X that…' — the fixed cleft frame.
Non-defining relative about people after the comma.
The eggs were located in the canes.
Absolute phrase: its monopoly broken, Byzantium rebuilt.
Fronted inversion: 'Such was the demand that…'.

gaps.hint: preposition: owes its name ___ this material
gaps.explanation: 'Owe something to something' — the source takes 'to'.
